title: CLAUDE.md
text: Four source files R/: load_data.R — Core functionality. load_cps() reads per-year .feather files local directory, selects columns via tidy evaluation (... forwarded dplyr::select), row-binds years together. Convenience wrappers load_org(), load_basic(), load_may(), load_org_sample() set sample name. extracts directory can passed .extracts_dir set via environment variables (EPIEXTRACTS_CPSORG_DIR, EPIEXTRACTS_CPSBASIC_DIR, EPIEXTRACTS_CPSMAY_DIR). download_data.R — download_cps() downloads .tar.gz archives microdata.epi.org extracts locally. metadata.R — cps_version() cps_citation() read version/citation attributes stored loaded data. assert_cps_version() validates specific version. checks.R — Internal validation helpers: valid_sample_name() assert_valid_extract().

title: CLAUDE.md
text: Documentation roxygen2-based (edit man/*.Rd NAMESPACE hand). README.md generated README.Rmd — edit .Rmd source. Sample/demo data lives inst/extdata/ zstd-compressed .feather files, generated data-raw/sample_data.R (loads real ORG extracts, regenerating requires configured extracts directory). Full-year samples cover 2023–2025; single-month file epi_cpsorg_sample_1979_1.feather exists fixture monthly/partial-year messaging tests. CI via GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml) builds pkgdown site push master.

title: Tools to use Economic Policy Institute Microdata Extracts
text: First, install current version package R-Universe: add EPI r-universe repo .Rprofile can simply download CPS microdata using download_cps(). example, download latest EPI CPS ORG extracts .feather format https://microdata.epi.org place directory C:\data\cps. data downloaded, load selection CPS data analysis: See vignette("epiextractr") examples.
code: install.packages(   "epiextractr",    repos = c("https://economic.r-universe.dev", getOptions("repos")) ) # Example .Rprofile options(repos = c(   epi = "https://economic.r-universe.dev",   getOption("repos") )) install.packages("epiverse") download_cps("org", "C:\data\cps") load_cps("org", 2000:2019, year, orgwgt, wage, wbho, .extracts_dir = "C:\data\cps")
